subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What should `/new` and `/reset` do in a multi-agent channel when the user does not specify an agent target, and what target syntax should be supported across text and native slash commands?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe default and authorization model affect session state, command UX, and channel-specific native command registration, so automation should not choose the contract alone.

options.title: Require explicit target
options.body: Require an explicit agent/account target in ambiguous multi-agent rooms and return a chooser or refusal when no target is provided.

options.title: Choose active agent
options.body: Pick the active or highest-context agent for no-target commands, improving convenience but risking surprising resets.

options.title: Reset active participants
options.body: Reset all agents participating in the current thread, preserving group-room semantics but making broad reset behavior intentional.

recommendation.title: Require explicit target
recommendation.body: Require an explicit agent/account target in ambiguous multi-agent rooms and return a chooser or refusal when no target is provided.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history signal on the shared native command/session target contract that this decision would change.
